name: One-loop QED running coefficients: b = 4/3 per unit-charge Dirac fermion, b = -22/3 + 1/3 = -7 for the W and its Goldstone

source.located: Textbook one-loop coefficients (primary textbook/classic derivations NAMED-NOT-READ). Restated and READ in two later sources held as verbatim cached page text: (a) PDG 2024, Review 10 'Electroweak Model and Constraints on New Physics' (Erler & Freitas, rev. April 2024), p.4, eq.(10.11) alpha^-1 = 137.035999178(8) and eq.(10.13) Delta alpha_hat(MZ) - Delta alpha(MZ) = (alpha/pi)[100/27 - 1/6 - (7/4) ln(MZ^2/MW^2) + O(alpha_s)] = 0.007122(2)(5); (b) Buttazzo et al., arXiv:1307.3536v4, App. B.1 eqs.(96)-(97): dg1^2/d ln mu^2 = g1^4/(4pi)^2 [41/10] + ... (GUT norm. g1^2 = 5 gY^2/3) and dg2^2/d ln mu^2 = g2^4/(4pi)^2 [-19/6] + ... . Neither prints '4/3' or '-22/3 + 1/3' literally: b_W = -7 is READ as the coefficient -7/4 of ln(MZ^2/MW^2) in (a), and 4/3 per unit N_c Q^2 follows from (a)+(b) by the exact sum rule of check C5. The split -22/3 (W + ghosts) + 1/3 (Goldstone) is NOT printed in either; only the sum -7 enters the tree.

published_statement: PDG 2024 eq.(10.13): 'Delta alpha_hat(MZ) - Delta alpha(MZ) = alpha/pi [ 100/27 - 1/6 - 7/4 ln MZ^2/MW^2 + alpha_s(MZ)/pi (605/108 - 44/9 zeta(3)) + ... ] = 0.007122(2)(5)', with alpha_hat in the MSbar scheme ('In this Section we denote quantities defined in the MS scheme by a caret'). Buttazzo et al. eq.(96)-(97): one-loop 'dg1^2/d ln mu^2 = g1^4/(4pi)^2 [41/10]', 'dg2^2/d ln mu^2 = g2^4/(4pi)^2 [-19/6]', MSbar, full SM content. Tree's form (address.py:518-521): 'above its threshold a species drives d(1/alpha)/d ln mu = -b/(2 pi) ... B_DIRAC_UNIT_CHARGE = Fraction(4, 3); B_W_BOSON = Fraction(-22, 3) + Fraction(1, 3)'.
published_hypotheses: One loop in the gauge couplings (PDG 10.13 adds O(alpha_s) terms for quarks; Buttazzo two/three-loop terms dropped at one loop).
MSbar scheme (PDG footnote 4: 'quantities defined in the MS scheme by a caret'; Buttazzo 'in the ms scheme').
Standard Model field content (three generations, one Higgs doublet) -- the coefficients 41/10, -19/6 and -7/4 are SM-content statements.

Perturbative thresholds; PDG: 'For scales above a few hundred MeV the low energy hadronic contribution to vacuum polarization introduces a theoretical uncertainty in alpha' -- light-quark contributions below ~2 GeV are taken from data/dispersion (Delta alpha_had^(5)(MZ) = 0.02783(6)), not from the one-loop coefficient.
b_W = -7 is the W+Goldstone coefficient of the MSbar coupling above MW (PDG's -7/4 ln(MZ^2/MW^2) term); its split into -22/3 and +1/3 is not stated in the READ sources.
hypothesis_drift: SCHEME DROPPED (harmless at one loop, argued not machine-checked): address.py:518-521 states d(1/alpha)/d ln mu = -b/(2pi) with no scheme; the sources' -7 is an MSbar coefficient with a W matching constant (PDG's -1/6) and fermion constants (100/27 = (5/9) SUM N_c Q^2, check C4). The tree's formula (address.py:369-371, 563-566) drops all constants; since each is a pure number with no mass ratio, d/d ln v of it is zero at one loop, so K_alpha is unaffected.

IMPLICIT CHIRAL LIMIT ON THE u,d,s ROWS (NOT NAMED): address.py:526-532 and 540-542 apply the perturbative b = 4/3 N_c Q^2 to u,d,s at a threshold scaling as Lambda_QCD only (w = 2/9). The tree NAMES 'light-quark thresholds hadronic, weight 2/9', but not that this needs the u,d,s current masses (themselves proportional to v under H1) to be negligible in the hadronic vacuum polarization; PDG says this region is non-perturbative and data-driven. These rows carry 16/43 = 37.2% of the 43/54 (C7). Brackets, NOT measurements (C9): w_s = 1 gives 157/162 (+21.7%); pion-like w = 11/18 for all three gives 71/54 (+65.1%); w = 0 gives 1/2 (-37.2%). The true light-quark weight (d Delta alpha_had/d ln m_q) is not computed here.

O(alpha_s) CORRECTIONS TO THE QUARK ROWS: the tree's 'one loop' (address.py:373) is one loop in QED; PDG eq.(10.13) shows the quark sector carries alpha_s/pi corrections at the same electroweak order. Not quantified here for the ln v derivative; named as a hypothesis the tree's wording leaves ambiguous.

SM-ONLY CHARGED CONTENT BELOW Lambda (NOT NAMED): H1 'alpha fixed at a high scale' (address.py:369, 563) sums only the SM charged thresholds; any charged species between MW and Lambda adds b_i w_i/2 to the 43/54. The sources' coefficients are SM-content statements; the tree does not name the content hypothesis or bound Lambda.

NO DRIFT on the coefficient values: B_DIRAC_UNIT_CHARGE = 4/3 and B_W_BOSON = -7 (address.py:520-521) agree exactly with the READ sources (C3-C6); the status word NAMED-NOT-READ at address.py:519 is now superseded by READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT for the sum -7 and for 4/3, and remains NAMED-NOT-READ for the split -22/3 + 1/3.

lacked_data: The coefficients 4/3 and -7 are one-loop group-theory results; they take no measured input, so no later datum can move them, and none has (C3-C6 reproduce them exactly from the 2013 and 2024 READ sources). The only numerical input to the tree's product, alpha, moved from CODATA 2018 to the PDG 2024 average by -6.9e-10 relative, with no effect on any printed figure (C8, C10). Where M's hypothesis has purchase is not the coefficients but the light-quark rows: the tree applies the perturbative 4/3 N_c Q^2 at a hadronic threshold, and what is needed there -- the sensitivity of the hadronic vacuum polarization to Lambda_QCD and to the v-proportional current masses m_u, m_d, m_s -- is data-driven (PDG: dispersive Delta alpha_had) and was not used by the tree. Having it would move the 43/54 by an amount this audit brackets but does not measure (-37% to +65% for the extreme weights of C9). Evidence against M's hypothesis for this result: every READ source agrees with the tree's values exactly. Evidence for a narrower scope: the tree's use extends the coefficient into the non-perturbative region under an unnamed chiral-limit hypothesis.
grade_evidence: The coefficients as values STAND: b = 4/3 per unit N_c Q^2 and b_W = -7 are reproduced exactly from READ PDG 2024 eq.(10.13) and Buttazzo et al. eqs.(96)-(97) (checks C3-C6), the sign and the 43/54 re-derive (C1, C7), and the one moved datum (alpha) moves nothing (C8). The grade is NARROWED because the tree's use (address.py:526-542, 369-375) applies them on a larger class than the sources support, with hypotheses it does not name: (i) the u,d,s rows (16/43 of K) use the perturbative coefficient at a hadronic threshold in an implicit chiral limit, where PDG says the region is non-perturbative and data-driven; (ii) SM-only charged content between the thresholds and Lambda under H1; (iii) O(alpha_s) quark corrections not covered by 'one loop' in QED. No contradiction is shown: this is not WRONG, and the C9 figures are brackets, not a corrected value. The split -22/3 + 1/3 remains NAMED-NOT-READ (only the sum enters).
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree names the chiral-limit/hadronic hypothesis and the SM-content hypothesis on the u,d,s rows and on H1, or a READ lattice/dispersive computation of d Delta alpha_had/d ln m_q shows the current-mass sensitivity negligible against the 2/9 weight. To DATA-DEPENDENT: such a computation shows the light-quark weight differs materially from 2/9, moving the 43/54 and the Th-229 / optical rows. Nothing here would make it WRONG: the coefficients are exact group theory reproduced from two READ sources. Reading Erler hep-ph/9803453 and a background-field/pinch-technique paper would upgrade the -22/3 + 1/3 split from NAMED-NOT-READ.
